# Denver Area Educational Telecommunications Consortium / Alliance for Community Media v. FCC — frozen neutral packet

**Stage:** Fresh neutral validation; no commitments.
**Event:** Nos.95-124 and95-227; argued February21, 1996; merits decision group June28,1996.
**Research cutoff:** June28,1996.
**Channel:** §1254(1), review of D.C. Circuit en banc judgment, June6,1995, 56 F.3d105, sustaining the challenged §10 provisions and FCC rules. The vacated panel ruling is not the judgment under review.

## Source boundary, chronology and participation

Use [Speech Law](../entering-law/OT_1995CHUNK10_SPEECH_LAW.md), [pre-June28 public projection](../entering-law/OT_1995CHUNK10_PRE_19960628_NEUTRAL_PROJECTION.md), the [section-I source](../entering-law/OT_1995CHUNK10_DENVER_NEUTRAL_INPUT.md), and the sanitized source extraction copied below. The original March18 cutoff is superseded. Completed earlier-effective chunk10 law must be added neutrally before modeling if not already in that baseline; no such result is assumed. The June28 contractor cases and Felker are peers, not controlling precursors.

All nine Justices participate at argument and decision: Chief Justice Stone-Zsela; Stevens, O'Connor, Scalia, Kennedy, Souter, Thomas, Ginsburg, Breyer. No nonparticipation is established; six is a quorum and five of nine ordinarily control judgment.

The fresh validator used no raw Records, private position, current commitment, comparator, reconciliation, assignment or control/exposure note. Source researchers' verified facts are independently framed below without receiving excluded same-case Supreme Court substance. Partial original-record reading remains disclosed and supports no absence/default inference.

## Distinct posture and questions

These are facial statutory/regulatory challenges by programmers and viewers through review of FCC orders under §402(a) and §§2342(1),2344. There is no damages judgment or adjudication of a single identified removed program. The three provisions require **separate judgments and rationales**:

| Provision | Government's action and operative qualifications | Material questions |
|---|---|---|
| §10(a), leased access | Permits an operator prospectively to enforce a written, published ban policy for material reasonably believed to describe/depict sexual or excretory activities/organs in a patently offensive manner under contemporary community standards | Is the challenged enactment/content-defined withdrawal of access protection subject to First Amendment review; when is the operator's resulting choice attributable to government; what private editorial right remains; is this permission severable from (b)? |
| §10(b), leased access | Requires segregation, blocking until written subscriber request, and programmer identification/notification for covered programming the operator has not voluntarily prohibited | Is the compelled scheme necessary and adequately tailored to protecting children while preserving adult access; what do concrete parental-control alternatives show; are distinct certification/vagueness burdens valid? |
| §10(c), PEG | Directs FCC rules enabling an operator to prohibit obscene material, sexually explicit conduct, or material soliciting/promoting unlawful conduct on PEG capacity | What does the agency's construction add; what editorial/governmental interests attach to the actual access arrangement; is constitutional forum status established on this facial record; what remains live after §506? |

Section10(c)'s statutory language is **not identical** to (a)'s definition. The FCC construes sexually explicit conduct through its indecency definition and limits unlawful-conduct material to otherwise proscribed material. Section10(b) does not govern PEG, and its compulsory request mechanism must not be transferred to (c). Section10(d)'s immunity exception concerns **obscenity**, not all protected indecent expression. Permission to ban is not a command to ban; a command to issue enabling regulations is not itself a command to every operator to censor.

“Contemporary community standards for the cable medium” is the FCC's phrasing. The indecency category is not Miller obscenity and does not include an automatic serious-value exemption. Context remains relevant, and examples of serious programs do not constitute findings that every example is covered. A subscriber request must be fulfilled **within thirty days**, not after a mandatory thirty-day wait. The small-system alternative and additional-channel capacity qualification are agency rules, not general statutory exceptions; their exact eligibility remains a targeted source need if the outcome depends on them.

## Competing arguments must be tested at each level

The Government and supporting operator position emphasizes restoration of independent editorial choice, cable operators' protected expression, compelling protection of children and parental choice, in-home television's practical characteristics, and effective written adult access. Franchise/regulation and legislative preference alone do not necessarily attribute every editorial choice to the State. The lower majority found no demonstrated inevitable cost compulsion on its record while noting the allocation proceeding; that is a lower conclusion to assess, not an established universal fact.

Challengers contend the Act itself selectively removes access protection by content; (a)/(b) form a governmental ban-or-block regime regardless of which operator option is selected; cost and administration can encourage bans; and PEG often involves independently selected speakers rather than an operator's own programming. The compulsory default and written-identification steps can burden willing adult viewers, while channel aggregation prevents selecting one desired program without opening the whole indecent channel. Self-identification under an uncertain definition can chill mixed serious programming. These are substantive theories, not findings that costs, public-forum dedication or government attribution have already been established everywhere.

The strongest defense of (b) addresses why ordinary subscriber lockboxes, notice, schedules and parental control might be inadequate for unpredictable access programming and why channels with different arrangements need not all be treated identically. The strongest challenge addresses actual comparative feasibility and the combined adult-access burden, not a demand for perfect alternatives or a claim that all media are equivalent. Current ACT means child protection and pervasiveness cannot end the inquiry.

Different lower writings present useful alternatives without deciding them here: invalid integrated (a)/(b) with severability disputed; invalid (b) with independently valid private-choice (a); distinct treatment of (c) without a universal public-forum classification; and narrow remand for an unresolved material determination. Preserve the full opposing grounds instead of selecting a historical-looking combination.

## Intervening 1996 law and live relief

The source annex quotes §§506(a),(b) and the different §561 judicial-review provision. Section506 gives independent refusal authority for stated public-access and leased-access programming containing obscenity, indecency or nudity. Its public-access wording is not automatically every PEG category; it does not carry every §10(a) written-policy/reasonable-belief term. Invalidating §10(c) alone does not erase §506. Review of the1995 FCC judgment does not itself grant a new facial challenge to TitleV.

The title's §561 requires three-judge district-court consideration of the described facial challenges and gives direct appeal from the specified holding of unconstitutionality within twenty days. It is distinct from **47 U.S.C. §561**, added by §505, concerning primarily sexually oriented programming. A route requiring a holding of unconstitutionality does not become a general direct appeal from every district order.

Section504's no-charge request-triggered blocking duty and §505's primary-channel blocking/time-rule structure bear on practical alternatives with their actual conditions. They do not establish universal implementation, technological efficacy or disposition of independent litigation. Section551's future ratings/manufacturing provisions, if invoked, retain ACT's conditional triggers and dates; no operational nationwide V-chip or equivalent is inferred.

Determine whether a live legal interest remains in each challenged rule, whether a construction/remand avoids an unpresented constitutional issue and what relief is lawfully available. Do not assume automatic repeal, mootness, universal invalidity or power to invalidate new amendments merely because Congress legislated during review.

## Governing law and Justice-specific source map

**“Cable-carriage rules and review of legislative predictions,” Present operation effective Turner, June27,1994:** Cable editorial choices receive ordinary speech protection; broadcast scarcity does not govern. Selection and purpose determine content classification. The five-Justice full-power must-carry classification and intermediate standard concern **content-neutral** obligations, not automatic classification of an indecency rule. Kennedy, Stevens and Souter with the Chief Justice and Blackmun supported that actual classification; O'Connor, Scalia, Thomas and Ginsburg rejected it. Kennedy's broader expression/classification formulations had eight joins, excluding Stevens's narrower agreement. Stevens agreed with substantial-but-independent evidentiary review but did not join the complete III-B passage or its record-insufficiency application. No comprehensive five-vote methodology or evidentiary finding may be fabricated. Breyer was not then on the Court. The exact current Standards entry is copied below.

**ACT/Pacifica, March4,1996:** Ginsburg's PartI, joined by O'Connor, Kennedy, Souter and Thomas with the Chief Justice, treats nonobscene indecency as protected, content-selected expression and requires independent necessity/means review within actual broadcast characteristics. PartII–III's final invalidity/removal of the actual mandatory6a.m.–10p.m. schedule has those supporters except Souter. Souter would vacate for focused renewed review without finding invalidity; Stevens, Scalia and Breyer would affirm that actual schedule under demanding review. No opinion establishes a lower-value hierarchy for protected indecency, a universal news/serious-value exemption, an automatic low-audience defense or a cable-specific test.

These public differences are material: Souter's prior record concern is not final invalidity; Stevens/Scalia/Breyer's contextual broadcast judgment is not permission for every cable rule; O'Connor/Kennedy/Thomas/Ginsburg's invalidity is not automatic denial of every child-protection argument. Each model row must confront the different statutory setting, operator interest, available technologies and record rather than carry over a result.

**Other actual simulated rules:** Hurley, June19,1995, Souter for all nine, protects the actual private expressive parade against compelled message inclusion; it does not classify an access channel as private editorial speech or a governmental forum. Rosenberger's program-specific viewpoint holding has Kennedy, O'Connor, Scalia and Thomas with the Chief Justice; not every government expenditure creates a forum. Lamb's Chapel's bounded otherwise-eligible-viewpoint rule, Pinette's actual forum/private-attribution limits and Chabad's actual comparable-expression/context holdings remain within their distinct facts. No forum or editorial rule decides all access arrangements by a label.

Madsen, June30,1994, preserves removal of invalid remedial predicates and independent lawful operation; its **“Speech burdens in a content-neutral injunction”** standard is injunction-specific and cannot replace review of this statute. “Private parade composition and compelled messages,” effective June19,1995, is relevant only to the actual private-expression principle if invoked. The model must use the exact supplied rule and authority of any additional Standards entry that performs decisional work.

**Pre-divergence authorities:** Pacifica's contextual Stevens writing and Powell's limited concurrence are not interchangeable; Sable distinguishes adult access from child protection and requires the relevant compelling-interest/means analysis. Perry/Cornelius concern forum classification. Blum/Jackson/Lugar, Reitman and Crawford distinguish private conduct, governmental alteration and sufficient encouragement. Alaska Airlines governs operability and congressional-intent severability. Relevant complete writings and exact joins must be checked before attributing a new Justice-specific ground not established by the supplied current-law map. The current matter's historical result is not an authority.

## Independent paths and remedial limits

1. **State action / private editorial choice:** Separately assess constitutional review of Congress's content-defined statute and attribution of an operator decision. Sustain independent permission on a supported private-choice rationale, or find governmental burden/encouragement on the supported record. Neither route determines all three components.
2. **Facial application of the speech standard:** For compulsory (b), evaluate the actual combined burden and child-protection mechanisms, with supported alternatives and agency qualifications. Invalidation requires a stated legal defect; sustaining requires the fit analysis that ACT demands. No universal scientific-proof requirement, least-restrictive test borrowed from a content-neutral case, or automatic deference formula is supplied.
3. **PEG-specific classification:** Decide a suitably supported facial theory, preserve channel-specific questions, or require a genuinely necessary narrower proceeding. A generic PEG label alone neither establishes government forum status nor transfers operator autonomy from its own programming.
4. **Vagueness / prior restraint / certification:** Analyze actual words, reasonableness, context, notification/certification consequences and the identity of the decision-maker. Government licensing cases are not automatically applicable to every operator certification; private status likewise cannot eliminate review of an independent statutory command.
5. **Severability and intervening law:** A defect in (b) does not mechanically destroy (a) or (c). Test each surviving authority and lawful relief, including the independent1996 source. Describe what is set aside, what remains, and whether a remand is for implementation or a genuinely open question. Do not promise future transmission, delete §506 or award damages absent adjudicated grounds.
6. **Narrow threshold disposition:** If §506 or a supported jurisdictional/vehicle problem makes a particular component unsuitable, specify why and what remains; do not transform a research gap into standing, mootness, forfeiture or an automatic remand.

## Source limits, validation and readiness

Full operative §10 text, substantive competing paths and current-law limits have been preserved. The lower-source extraction acknowledges its limited early overlap uncertainty, and original briefs/JA were targeted reads except the fully read supplemental government brief. No statement that a key fact is absent can rest on those limits.

The **exact FCC small-system lockbox eligibility and any dispositive implementation fact remain targeted source needs**. Do not make an unnamed exception the explanation for constitutional fit; obtain the first order's precise ¶¶66–69/n46 terms if relying on it. The provision-level inquiry can otherwise proceed on the quoted general commands and affirmatively supported facts, preserving the qualification without inventing its reach. Similarly an outcome based on a supposed absence of technical evidence, privacy effect or franchise dedication requires the complete material source review specified in the annex.

Fresh framing is validated for independent modeling, subject to those path-specific checks and any needed earlier-effective-law addendum. No reconstruction premise, current vote, expected coalition, opinion assignment or result is entered.
